messages:
alex: quick spike — put up a prototype of a Tokenomics Explorer in the console: https://figma.com/file/xyz (mock). want fast feedback on what to show by default :eyes:

maya: took a look. love the per-model table. question: how are we calculating cache savings? estimated or from telemetry? :thinking_face:

alex: currently prototype uses telemetry-derived fields: `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cache_hits`, `tokens_saved_est`. tokens_saved_est = cache_hits * avg_cached_prefix_length (rough heuristic)

sam: big 👍 on using telemetry. caveat: sampling. our ingest only keeps full telemetry for 2% of requests to reduce cost. how do we avoid biased savings numbers?

maya: yeah sampling bias is real. we should use deterministic sampling keyed by `route_id` so rollouts/tenants are fairly represented. also expose sample_rate on UI so users know accuracy.

patrick: UI note — show both an "estimated" badge and a confidence band (e.g., ±X%) for any cost-savings metric. default timeframe 7d with toggle to 30d and custom. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: for attribution SQL (sketch):
```sql
SELECT
  route_id,
  model_name,
  sum(prompt_tokens+completion_tokens) AS tokens_total,
  sum(case when cache_hit then 0 else completion_tokens end) AS billed_tokens,
  sum(case when cache_hit then estimated_saved_tokens else 0 end) AS tokens_saved
FROM inference_events
WHERE sample_key_hash % 100 < sample_pct
GROUP BY route_id, model_name;
```

alex: nice. we also need to account for model-variant migration: if routing policy falls back from big-model -> small-model, the unit economics change. want a per-route per-model breakdown + a stacked timeline of routed fraction.

maya: agree. add `routed_to_model` and `policy` metadata to events. then UI can show: total tokens, tokens by model, effective $/1000 tokens by model, and total savings from caching + quantization.

sam: question: do we expose dollar figures by default? internal cost vs customer charge differ. maybe default to unit-cost (tokens * $unit) but allow toggle to show internal vs external pricing.

patrick: default to internal $/k tokens with a tooltip: "shown as internal inference cost; use chargeback view to map to billing prices". make the toggle sticky per org.

maya: implementation detail: caching types — prefix cache vs KV cache. prefix cache is deterministic by prompt hash; KV cache is sequence-level and harder to attribute. We should show separate lines: prefix_cache_savings, kv_cache_savings, and unexplained_gap.

alex: good call. also support a "what-if" slider: change cache_hit_rate from observed to 0/10/20% to show sensitivity on unit economics. helps infra/product decide where to invest.

sam: telemetry todo: add fields to event schema: `cache_type` (prefix|kv|none), `tokens_saved`, `cache_ttl_bucket`, `sample_rate`, `routed_model`, `policy_id`. keep payload < 1KB.

patrick: UX: in per-route detail, show top 3 contributing prompts with anonymized hashes and avg tokens to allow troubleshooting (no PII). add CTA: "Create eval set for regression" next to savings drop.

alex: ops-bot: create epic and attach telemetry schema + figma link?

ops-bot: created EPIC-4012 Tokenomics Explorer + telemetry (https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/EPIC-4012) — assigned to @alex, @maya, @sam. :white_check_mark:

maya: one more: rollout/feature flags. when a new routing policy deploys, surface a canary row that shows pre/post unit costs and % delta so product can rollback quickly if cost jumps.

sam: agree. we'll need pre-change snapshot (24h) and live comparison. sampling needs to be stable across snapshot and live to be comparable. use `sample_key` salted by deployment id during rollout.

patrick: final ask from me — export CSV + per-tenant API so growth can hook chargeback into finance tools. also include API pagination and route filters.

alex: awesome. i'll update prototype with confidence bands, cache breakdown, and the what-if slider. will post updated figma and SQL snippets here tomorrow. thanks all. :rocket:
